children.text: The best content marketing ideas for Saudi businesses focus on three things: writing in proper Arabic that sounds local, showing up where Saudis already spend time (short video, WhatsApp, and Google), and tying your message to moments people care about, like Ramadan, National Day, and the goals of Vision 2030. Do those well, and you build trust before you ever ask for a sale.
That is the short version. The rest of this guide breaks down each idea, who it works for, and how to start.
Why content marketing works so well in Saudi Arabia

The numbers make the case better than any pitch. Saudi Arabia has one of the most connected populations on earth. By the end of 2025, internet penetration reached about 99 percent, with roughly 34 million people online, according to DataReportal. Social media reach was even higher when counting multiple accounts per person.

Two things stand out for a business owner. First, almost everyone you want to reach is already on a screen. Second, the audience is young, mobile, and used to video. WhatsApp, Snapchat, TikTok, and Instagram all pull tens of millions of active users in the Kingdom. That is a rare combination: a huge digital crowd that is also comfortable buying, booking, and asking questions online.

Content marketing fits this perfectly. Instead of shouting an ad, you earn attention by being useful, entertaining, or both. You answer the question someone typed into Google at midnight. You make the short clip they send to a friend. Over time, that adds up to something paid ads cannot buy: a brand people actually like.

children.text: Content marketing ideas for Saudi businesses
Here are the ideas worth your time, roughly in the order most local brands should tackle them.
1. Write Arabic-first, not Arabic-translated
This is the one most foreign and even some local brands get wrong. Running English copy through a translator produces text that reads stiff and a little off. Saudi readers notice immediately.

Write for Arabic from the start. Let a native writer shape the tone, humour, and references. Modern Standard Arabic works for formal pieces, while a lighter, friendlier Saudi voice often performs better on social media. If you serve both Arabic and English speakers, build two versions that each feel natural, rather than one stretched to cover both.
2. Lean into short vertical video

Short video is the format Saudi audiences reward most. A thirty-second clip on TikTok, Snapchat Spotlight, or Instagram Reels can reach more people than a month of polished blog posts, and it costs far less than a TV shoot.

You do not need a studio. A clean phone video, decent light, and a clear point will do. Show how your product is made. Answer a common customer question on camera. Film a quick before and after. The goal is rhythm, so post often and learn what your audience replays and shares.
3. Build content around the Saudi calendar

Timing is half the battle. Ramadan is the single biggest content and commerce season of the year, and audiences expect brands to show up with warmth, generosity, and a slower, more reflective tone. Plan that campaign months, not the week before.

Beyond Ramadan, map your year to Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Saudi National Day on September 23, Founding Day in February, and back to school. Each one is a natural reason to publish something timely without feeling like a hard sell.

children.text: 4. Answer real customer questions in writing

Every business gets the same handful of questions on the phone and in DMs. Turn each one into a short, clear article or page. “How much does X cost in Riyadh?” “Do you deliver to Jeddah?” “What is the difference between these two services?”

This is the heart of search-friendly content. When you answer the exact question people type, you show up when they search, and you save your team from repeating themselves. It also feeds answer engines and AI assistants, which increasingly pull short, direct answers straight from pages like these.
5. Use WhatsApp as a content channel, not just support

WhatsApp is woven into daily life in Saudi Arabia, yet most businesses only use it to reply to complaints. Treat it as a publishing channel instead. Send a short weekly tip, a new arrival, an exclusive offer, or a quick voice note from the founder.
Keep it opt in and keep it valuable. A list of people who chose to hear from you is worth more than a much larger audience that scrolls past your posts.
6. Partner with local creators

Influencer content carries real weight in the Kingdom, and the creator scene is deep across food, travel, gaming, beauty, and family life. The trick is fit over follower count. A creator with 30,000 engaged local followers in your niche often beats a celebrity with millions of distant ones.
Give creators room to make content in their own voice. Audiences can spot a stiff, scripted ad, and they trust the creator far less the moment it feels forced.
7. Tell local success stories and case studies
Saudis respond to proof from people like them. A short case study, a customer testimonial, or a behind the scenes look at a real project builds more confidence than any list of features.
Name the city. Show the face. Share the actual result. A bakery in Khobar, a clinic in Riyadh, a contractor in Dammam: specific, local detail makes the story believable and easy to relate to.
8. Create how-to and educational content

Teaching builds authority. A real estate firm can explain the home buying process step by step. A salon can post styling tips. A SaaS company can publish short tutorials. When you help people understand something, you become the name they remember when they are ready to buy.
This content also ages well. A solid guide can bring in search traffic for years with the occasional update, which makes it one of the better returns in your whole content budget.
9. Tie your message to Vision 2030 themes

Vision 2030 shapes the national conversation, from tourism and entertainment to sustainability, local manufacturing, and women in the workforce. Brands that connect to these themes in an honest way tap into real momentum.

The key word is honest. Audiences reward genuine alignment and quickly tire of buzzwords stapled onto an unrelated product. Show how your work actually supports a bigger goal, then let the story speak.
10. Publish thought leadership on LinkedIn for B2B

If you sell to other businesses, LinkedIn deserves attention. The platform’s local audience keeps growing, and decision makers are there. Founder and executive posts, short market insights, and lessons from real projects tend to outperform corporate announcements.
Write like a person, not a press office. One clear idea, a bit of perspective, and a real example will travel further than a glossy company update.

children.text: Make your content findable: SEO, AEO, and GEO
Great content that no one finds is a wasted effort. Three overlapping practices help people and machines discover your work.
SEO (search engine optimization)

is the classic one. Use the words your customers actually search, in Arabic and English. Write clear page titles, useful headings, and a strong opening that states what the page delivers. Claim and complete your Google Business Profile for every location, since local search drives a lot of walk in and call in business across Saudi cities.
AEO (answer engine optimization)

is about being the source that answers the question. Lead pages with a short, direct answer, then expand. Use plain question headings like the ones in this guide. Add an FAQ section. This format is exactly what voice assistants and featured snippets pull from.
GEO (generative engine optimization)

is the newest layer. AI tools now summarize the web and cite sources when people ask for recommendations. To earn a place in those answers, make your facts clear and easy to lift, keep information current, and state things plainly rather than burying them in fluff. Structured, well organized content gives these systems clean material to quote.
The good news is that all three reward the same habits: clear structure, real answers, fresh information, and content built for humans first.
How to measure what is working

Pick a few numbers that map to your goals and ignore the vanity metrics. For awareness, track reach, video views, and shares. For interest, watch website visits, time on page, and WhatsApp opt ins. For sales, follow leads, bookings, and revenue tied to specific campaigns.

Review monthly, not daily. Content compounds, so give pieces time to find their audience before you judge them. Double down on the formats and topics that keep performing, and quietly retire the ones that do not.
Frequently asked questions
What is the most effective content marketing channel in Saudi Arabia?

There is no single winner, but short vertical video on TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram delivers the widest reach for most consumer brands, while WhatsApp drives the strongest direct engagement. B2B companies usually see the best results on LinkedIn.
Should Saudi businesses publish content in Arabic or English?

Arabic should lead for almost every local audience, written by a native speaker rather than translated. Add English when you serve expats, tourists, or international clients, and treat it as a separate version that reads naturally on its own.
How often should a Saudi business post content?

Consistency beats volume. For social video, three to five posts a week is a healthy target for many brands. For blogs and guides, one strong, well researched piece a week outperforms several thin ones.
Is Ramadan really that important for content marketing?
Yes. Ramadan is the peak season for attention, spending, and emotional connection in the Kingdom. Plan the campaign well in advance and lead with a warm, generous tone rather than aggressive selling.
How long does content marketing take to show results?

Social video can spark engagement within weeks, while search-driven content usually takes three to six months to build steady traffic. The payoff is durable, since good content keeps working long after you publish it.
Final word

Content marketing in Saudi Arabia rewards brands that respect the audience: write real Arabic, show up in video and on WhatsApp, build around the moments people care about, and answer the questions buyers are already asking. Start with two or three ideas from this list, do them consistently, and let the results guide where you invest next.
Pick one idea today. Film one clip, write one answer page, or plan one Ramadan campaign. Momentum starts with the first post.
